title: How a P-Trap Prevents Sewer Gas Backflow
description: A P-trap operates on a simple hydraulic principle to isolate indoor spaces from drain gases. Located directly beneath sink basins, the curved section retains a self-replenishing body of water after every use. This standing water forms an airtight physical barrier that stops volatile gases from traveling up from the sewer line. Simultaneously, incoming wastewater creates sufficient momentum to push old water and light debris over the weir and down the waste pipe. Proper trap depth and atmospheric venting ensure the seal stays intact without siphoning during drainage.

How a P-Trap Prevents Sewer Gas Backflow

A P-trap operates on a simple hydraulic principle to isolate indoor spaces from drain gases. Located directly beneath sink basins, the curved section retains a self-replenishing body of water after every use. This standing water forms an airtight physical barrier that stops volatile gases from traveling up from the sewer line. Simultaneously, incoming wastewater creates sufficient momentum to push old water and light debris over the weir and down the waste pipe. Proper trap depth and atmospheric venting ensure the seal stays intact without siphoning during drainage.
